title: The Errand
summary: Into the city with the docket. The instrument makers laugh and send them to Manako, who was hazed the same way once and shows them how to win.
goal: They have been laughed at, met Manako, heard his plan for the vial, and chosen how to file it.
howToPlay: Warm, funny and safe: a humiliation that turns into a win. **Nothing here hints at who he really is.**

intro.where: The city: an instrument makers' workshop, then a tea house a few streets on.
intro.readAloud: Off the train, the city is loud and close: cranes working behind the rooftops, a tram grinding past, a man arguing with a delivery van. The harbour is two streets over, and you can smell it. Your new uniforms are very obviously new.
intro.landmark: The harbour, two streets over, always in earshot.

carriesIn.when: If anyone has the tram map
carriesIn.then: They find the workshop without asking anyone.

carriesIn.when: If anyone saw a violet mark on the road in
carriesIn.then: They may recognise the next one.

position.note: In the city: the workshop and the tea house are a few streets apart.

brief.wants: Six uniforms away from her bench, nicely.
brief.opensWith: She reads the docket twice, then laughs.

willDiscuss.note: "Love, we make the vials. There's nothing in the bubble. That's the whole point of the bubble."
"Ask Manako. Tea house, a few streets on, corner table. He'll enjoy beating it."
She will, and it isn't cheap: "You'd be paying for his joke, love. Ask Manako first."

willNotDiscuss.why: Professional, not secretive: "Customers' business is customers' business."

voice.register: Brisk and amused by uniforms. Repeats a request back flattened, like a form.
samples: "That's not a thing. I've been here nineteen years and that's not a thing."

brief.statblock: Proposed: level 1, an instrument maker, non-combat.

cast.label: Manako
cast.role: Owns the tea house. A chemist, long retired.

brief.wants: To help these six win, and to be listened to while he does it.
brief.opensWith: He's already looking at the docket in their hands: "May I? ...Ah. They've sent you for the bubble."

willDiscuss.note: "Manako. I was a chemist, a long time ago. For them, as it happens."
Bitter, and fair with it: "They're not wicked. They're just very good at not talking."
Happily and at length, until he catches himself: "Sorry. You asked one question and I've given you four."
The vial: see the plan beat.

willDiscuss.topic: Who sent him for the bubble
willDiscuss.note: "My section officer, long retired now. They hand it down like a watch."

willNotDiscuss.why: He knows exactly what they are. He shrugs: "Somebody's sign for something. The city's full of them."
"They decided I'd made a fool of myself. Maybe I had." Then he changes the subject.

voice.register: Unhurried and warm, an old teacher's voice. Handles a thing before he talks about it. Goes over old failures out loud, then apologises.
samples: "Don't go back empty-handed. That's the whole joke, and you don't have to be in it."
"That's not a new joke. It was old when they played it on me."

brief.statblock: Not built. He can't be fought or caught in this scene.

beats.text: Read the city as they come off the train, then let them find the instrument makers.
beats.note:
Plant: A side street the dogs won't walk down, and a roof with no pigeons on it. Say nothing about it.
If they pass the harbour square: The gnoll statue, with HYUCK on the plaque.
If they wander instead: A tram, the harbour, and somewhere a clock striking five. The docket still says nineteen hundred.
Secret: Animals hear the Watcher's swarm as a high buzzing, and it's thick on that street.

beats.text: The instrument maker reads the docket twice and laughs. On any result, she sends them on to Manako. <trig id="docket-no-such-part"/>
beats.readAloud: "Love, we make the vials. There's nothing in the bubble. That's the whole point of the bubble. It's the bit that isn't there."
beats.note: If anyone tries to talk her round: Offer the check: it decides how warmly she sends them on.

beats.text: On the walk to the tea house: a small deep-violet mark at head height, on a tram-stop wall. Offer the check.
beats.note:
Plant: The same violet, at the same height, as on the road in. Say nothing about it.
Secret: Cicada's, like the others.

beats.text: Manako owns the tea house. He reads the docket before they finish explaining: "Ah. They've sent you for the bubble." <trig id="manako-at-his-table"/>
beats.readAloud: The tea house is small, warm and full: steam, low voices, a counter polished by a century of elbows. The regulars nod to the old man at the corner table as they pass, and his tea arrives without his asking.
beats.direction: Kind, useful and openly bitter about the Directorate, at an even pace. He gives his name before he's asked.
beats.note:
Watch for: Every line of his is a leak risk. If unsure, have him talk chemistry.
Secret: He founded Cicada. Nothing shows it here, because here he is only kind.

beats.text: If anyone watches the regulars rather than Manako, offer the check.
If anyone tries to place his name, offer the very hard knowledge check.

when.condition: someone tries to place the name

beats.text: If anyone watches Manako rather than the docket, offer the check.
Manako tells them how he came back empty-handed once, then gives them his plan. <trig id="docket-manakos-way"/>
beats.readAloud:
"They did this to me, you know. Forty-odd years ago. I came back with nothing, and they laughed, and I've had a long time to think about what I should have done."

"So. He's written BUBBLE, ONE. Don't argue with him. Take him at his word. The bubble lives in a sealed vial, and the vial is a real part, with a real number, and it isn't cheap. Requisition a new vial against this docket, exactly as he wrote it. It needs a signature from a desk above his, and it makes a form that says who asked for it, and why."

"You'll have done exactly what you were told. Somebody upstairs will spend four minutes of their afternoon working out why."
beats.note: Do: He writes the part number on the back of a bill for them, in a careful, old-fashioned hand. Grant it.

beats.text: Ask the table how they'll file the requisition. Let them settle it between themselves.

options.label: Quietly.
options.consequence: A receipt for Vetch, and nobody else the wiser.

options.label: So people see.
options.blurb: File it somewhere people will notice.
options.consequence: Filed where it's noticed: the base has heard by supper.

beats.text: Before they go, if it hasn't come up, he asks who they work for, and says one true thing about them.
beats.readAloud: "They dig things up, you know, the people you work for. Whatever they find goes in a vault, and nobody talks about it again. That's not wicked, mind. Some things ought to be locked away. But keeping quiet gets to be a habit."

beats.text: He asks them to come back and say how it went. If one was especially kind, he writes them his number on a napkin. <trig id="docket-tell-manako"/>
beats.note:
Do: Your call who, if anyone. No roll. Hand that player a note with the number.
Secret: Trainee messages are read: by the Directorate, as routine, and by the Watcher.

triggers.label: Docket: tell Manako how it went

beats.text: If someone refused the docket, the Deputy Director hears them in his office while the others are in the city. Cut between the two.
beats.readAloud: "Sit down. Section Officer Vetch says you refused a direct order. Tell me why."
beats.note:
Do: Let them make their case in their own words, then offer the check. He answers the argument they actually make.
If they ask what happens now: "It goes on your file. If you prove right, that goes on it too, in my hand."
If the order was badly given: He takes it up with Vetch himself, never in front of a candidate.

artefacts.title: A part number on the back of a bill
artefacts.gmNote: His handwriting, kept: it can be set against Cicada's papers much later.
artefacts.body: The back of a tea-house bill. In a careful, old-fashioned hand: a part number, a line under it, and replacement vial, levelling, sealed.

outro.endsWhen: They leave the tea house with a plan, a part number and the time.

tracks.why: If they were kind to him and someone got his number.

transition.line: The train back to the island, and the stores' requisitions hatch before nineteen hundred.

outro.onwards: The Train Back, to the island.
writeDown: Who holds Manako's number, if anyone.
Who heard what he said about the Directorate.

position.note: Leaving the city for the island.

temptations.text: Manako looks like a man who'd enjoy being asked a question about anything at all.

reactionPrompts.text: The humiliation turning into a win.
The table settling quietly or loudly on its own.

notes: Manako's scenes need care: every line is checked for leaks. He talks freely about everything except the Watcher, gives his real name, and is openly bitter about the Directorate and fatherly to recruits (D045). The Directorate has never linked the tea-house owner to Cicada, and both halves of that discovery belong to the players (D017, D034). The workshop and the tea house wait for Ingram's siting; the district is one where he has influence (D046).
